text:
Colorado hosts Nashville on a 7-2 loss at Columbus that ended its three-game winning streak, and the Avalanche are without Josh Manson and Zachary L'Heureux. Nashville beat Carolina 4-1 and is 3-1-1 in its last five. This is the second meeting this season. On Oct 25 the Predators won 6-2 and deserved it, taking 64% of simulated replays from the shots. Ross Colton and Jack Drury also play in Denver for the first time since leaving Colorado, though that isn't in our numbers.

Colorado has controlled more of the play. At five on five, the Avalanche have taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) to Nashville's 46%, and our model projects 3.34 to 2.82 tonight. The special teams are close, with Colorado slightly ahead on both sides. In net, Juuse Saros is projected for Nashville, +5.1 goals saved above expected this season after a -10.19 last year. Mackenzie Blackwood is projected for Colorado at -1.07, after +8.01 last season.

Nathan MacKinnon is 84% for a point and 40% to score, riding a six-game point streak. For Nashville, Filip Forsberg is 65% for a point with a five-game streak, and Ryan O'Reilly, a former Avalanche player, is at 61%. Our under-the-radar pick is T.J. Hughes, 43% for a point after moving into the top six with Jaden Schwartz and Brock Nelson, a line that creates chances (4.05 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice).
